title: Horta & Schiavon (2025)
subtitle: Modelling the density and mass of the Milky Way’s proto-galaxy
summary: This paper models the density and mass of the Milky Way's 'proto-galaxy' (centrally concentrated, metal-poor stars) using APOGEE-Gaia data, finding it follows a triaxial Plummer profile.

title: Han et al. (2022)
subtitle: The Stellar Halo of the Galaxy is Tilted and Doubly Broken
summary: This paper uses the H3 Survey to infer the shape and density profile of the Gaia-Sausage-Enceladus (GSE) stellar halo, finding it is best described by a tilted triaxial ellipsoid with a doubly broken power law.

parameters.Model: Tilted Triaxial Doubly Broken Power Law

title: Amarante et al. (2024)
subtitle: Mapping the anisotropic Galactic stellar halo with blue horizontal branch stars
summary: This study uses blue horizontal branch (BHB) stars from Legacy Survey photometric data to map the stellar halo density. This model version includes a 1 kpc constant density core to regularize the central density.

title: Chen et al. (2023)
subtitle: Mapping the milky way’s stellar halo with 2D data
summary: This paper proposes a new method for measuring the spatial density distribution of the stellar halo using the angular two-point correlation function (ATPCF) of RR Lyrae stars. They find a broken power-law profile with an oblate flattening factor, providing a robust measurement that is independent of individual star distances.

title: Yang et al. (2022)
subtitle: Constructing the Milky Way Stellar Halo in the Galactic Center by Direct Orbit Integration
summary: This study integrates the orbits of ~10,000 LAMOST K giants to construct the stellar halo density at all radii. They find that a double-broken power-law profile best describes the density, with breaks at 10 kpc and 25 kpc and a flattening factor that varies significantly with radius.
